title: A vendor bill makes Convert to No Charge ask where the cost goes
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location is connected to QuickBooks Online, with Inventory Asset and Cost of Parts mapped on its ShopView Accounts page, and that AccountingHub is not enabled.
  • Make sure the Goodwill category has a QuickBooks expense account at the test location.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, in status Approved, with one special-order part, part 1, received against it and its vendor bill of $125.00 entered.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Open the work order's three-dots menu.
  3. Click "Convert to No Charge".
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The menu shows "Convert to No Charge".

Step 3:

  • First a window titled "Change where the cost is posted?" opens.
  • Its text reads "The vendor bill for [part 1] ($125.00) was posted to Cost of Parts. If you continue, that cost moves to [account] when this work order is closed."
  • Its buttons are "Cancel" and "Continue".

Words in square brackets in a message stand for the value they name, such as the work order's number or the customer's name exactly as it is saved; every other word of the message must match exactly. [account] is the account the category picked in the next window is mapped to.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • S2-R8: “If a vendor bill already exists on the work order, a customer change (S2-R7), a Convert action (S2-R5, S2-R6) or, on a line that has a posted vendor bill, Mark as No Charge, Change category or Mark as Billable (Story 12) first shows the dialog "Change where the cost is posted?" with the body "The vendor bill for [part] ($[amount]) was posted to [account]. If you continue, that cost moves to [account] when this work order is [invoiced / closed]." For several bills: "The vendor bills for [n] parts ($[total]) were posted to [account]. ..." Buttons: Cancel and "Continue". The account names are the shop's own mapping rows (Cost of Parts, or the expense account of a category); between the expense accounts of two categories the dialog names both. Not shown when the location has no accounting integration.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Customer change, Convert or a line No Charge change with a vendor bill | "The vendor bill for [part] ($[amount]) was posted to [account]. If you continue, that cost moves to [account] when this work order is [invoiced / closed]." | Confirmation dialog, Cancel / Continue”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
